answer: Treat admission to an agent economy like a terrace farm: each new identity locks a bond that matures one step per epoch, the way yarrow slowly roots on a hillside. Voting weight grows only as bonds age, and peers can slash them for coordinated misbehavior. A sybil attacker running a thousand fake agents must freeze a thousand bonds for months before any counts, and can lose them all at once. Honest newcomers find an oasis with a modest, refundable deposit, while mass impersonation becomes slow and ruinous.
